newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-PowerGen pulls out of Bewag, sale threatened.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-PowerGen pulls out of Bewag, sale threatened.

text.p: British utility group PowerGen said on Wednesday it had withdrawn from the race to buy a stake in German state utility Berliner Kraft und Licht AG, pushing the government's privatisation plan one step closer to collapse.
The Berlin government had said it might be forced to relaunch the bidding process to privatise the company, known as Bewag, if the remaining foreign bidders pulled out of the race.

PowerGen, along with two U.S. groups and a consortium of German bidders was on the short-list of possible buyers for a 50.8 percent stake in the group. But on Wednesday PowerGen told Reuters it had decided against making a bid.

"We looked very closely at the commercial opportunities presented by the Bewag sale. However we have decided not to make a bid. And in the current circumstances it is unlikely that we will pursue our interest further in Bewag," PowerGen press officer Mike Pollak said by telephone from Britain.
Pollak declined to give specific reasons for the decision or comment further on when it had been taken.

But PowerGen's move narrows the field of candidates, which stood at nine late last year, and puts the Berlin government, eager to wrap up talks by the end of February for financial reasons, under considerable pressure.

Berlin's finance minister Annette Fugmann-Heesing, who had threatened to reopen the bidding if necessary, has made it clear she would favour an international buyer with long-term strategic interests in Bewag.
The Berlin government must sell 25.8 percent of its total 50.8 percent stake in Bewag by the end of February for financial reasons. The city's finance ministry had no immediate comment.

Industry sources said foreign bidders, including U.S. groups Enron and Southern Company, were unhappy about an existing contract between the city and PreussenElektra and Bayernwerk, both part of the German bidding consortium.

While a foreign buyer could obtain a majority stake in the Bewag, the group would not receive a majority on Bewag's supervisory board. A contract between Berlin and Bayernwerk and PreussenElektra promises them three seats on that board.
PreussenElektra and Bayernwerk, units of industrial giants VIAG AG and Veba AG, each already own a 10 percent stake in Bewag.
A sale to the German bidders could run afoul of cartel authorities, however, as VIAG and Veba already each own a 10 percent stake in Bewag, a cartel office spokeswoman said.
